verdicts.claim: Counsel was to read the licence files, README and homage wording, and clear the name, before the repo went public or anything was revealed.
verdicts.what_is_true: The repo was made public on its creation day by Orb's ruling (vision.md:80), and no file records any counsel review. Only forward-looking 'have counsel read' lines exist. Legal's later docs move the counsel read to before the store page (pre-store-checklist.md:37) or the first sale (steam-readiness.md:52, guide-licence-rundown.md:3), and the homage lines are gone from README and CLAUDE.md. The 'before public' precondition can no longer be met.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It keeps alive a 'breached' precondition that nobody can ever close, which adds worry and phase-gate noise.
verdicts.fix: Retire the 'before the repo goes public' counsel wording in licence-recommendation.md:3/161, public-readiness-edits.md:3, drafts/README.md:3/31, drafts/LICENSE-ASSETS:5 and suno-music.md:3. Keep one pre-sale counsel sitting, and settle whether it comes before the store page or before the first sale.

verdicts.claim: The repo was to stay private until the Must-fix edits, a rename, and Orb's licence and name approval were done; Must M6 places LICENSE, LICENSE-ASSETS, NOTICE, CONTRIBUTING and a PR template first.
verdicts.what_is_true: The repo is public with no LICENSE, NOTICE, CONTRIBUTING or PR template; licence files were added and then removed on 2026-09-29 (701c76a0, 31664705). Musts M1 to M5 are done: the repo is renamed, and the franchise, fan-game and old repo names are gone from the README, CLAUDE.md, the charters and the setup docs. README.md:7 reserves all rights and asks visitors not to copy. The repo has had 0 pull requests, and Legal's own go-to-market.md:350 says 'None of this is urgent'.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A breached 'do not make public' blocker reads as a live violation, even though no licence means all rights reserved, the most protective state for Orb.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record: close RL-020 for M1 to M5, fold M6 into the licence decision (AC-074) and a contributor note (AC-083), and drop 'Do not make the repo public without a licence file' from licence-register.md:86.

verdicts.claim: KAI is NO-GO as a shipped name; no KAI, VORR, Meridian or Calamity may be player-visible on any published build or clip, clips and promotion wait for neutral names, and no in-progress character art goes public.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule holds on the live build: the placeholder-name scan of the live index.pck finds 0 hits outside the allowlisted note and test fixture, the live pages have 0 hits, the pin shows PROTAGONIST and RIVAL, /prototype/ returns 404, and the holding page has no images. KAI, VORR, Meridian and Calamity remain only in public source (roster.js:5-6, prototype/index.html:185-186), which Legal itself rates a Should (S4). Marketing's go-to-market-plan.md:31 and :319 still say the live build shows KAI, which is stale.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low: keeping RL-002, RL-092 and RL-096 open, and Marketing's stale lines, keeps a promotion hold on a condition that is already met.
verdicts.fix: Close the shipped-name and clip-hold parts of RL-002, RL-092 and RL-096 with a pointer to the pack scan, correct go-to-market-plan.md:31 and :319, and keep the source rename as an S4 Should.

verdicts.claim: 'Orb Combat EX' is CONDITIONAL because of the live OrbCombat GitHub project; before any store page, itch.io page or first promotion, the formal search must be run (classes 9, 28, 41) with a same-day store re-check, '(working title)' kept and the pseudonym settled against the copyright line; Orb ruled the title stays.
verdicts.what_is_true: Cascachu/OrbCombat is live (GDScript, GPL-3.0, 0 stars, last push 2026-06-16, re-checked through the gh API today), and the formal register searches have never been run (name-screening.md:182). The holding page keeps '(working title)', but the /play/ page title does not. Public history (commit 701c76a0, an ancestor of origin/main) carries a real-name copyright line (name withheld here), so the pseudonym and holder question is already partly exposed.
verdicts.fix: Before any store or itch.io page, run the formal US, EU, UK and Japan search with a same-day store re-check, and decide the copyright-holder name. Add '(working title)' to the /play/ title. Marketing's wider 'every public page' scope is not Legal's rule and should be dropped.

verdicts.claim: No licence is chosen, so all rights are reserved; Legal recommends shape A; the README must say what visitors may do with a do-not-redistribute line; the missing licence blocks tips, sales, Steam and any 'open source' wording.
verdicts.what_is_true: There is no licence (GitHub's license field is null), and README.md:7 reserves all rights and asks visitors not to copy. An owner can sell or list an all-rights-reserved game without a licence file, and Legal's steam-readiness.md:37 calls the licence 'Orb's call', not a block. Only the 'open source' wording is truly barred, yet CLAUDE.md:3, which is public, says 'Free and open source'. The record contradicts itself (licence-recommendation.md:13, drafts/README.md:3 and vision.md:43 against vision.md:81), and README.md:7 says the hosted build is offline while /play/ serves a playable build.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Marketing treats a business choice as a hard block on Steam, sales and tips, which can stall plans while the real gaps (wrong public wording) go unfixed.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record: make the four licence statements agree with vision.md:81, drop 'Free and open source' from CLAUDE.md:3, fix README.md:7's 'offline' sentence, and keep 'licence first' only for outside contributions and open-source wording.

verdicts.claim: Rulings conflict: CLAUDE.md and name-screening say the Protagonist's collectibles must not be orbs, while q3-screen, fighter-concepts-review and tropes-and-folklore allow held orb fragments under six tripwires.
verdicts.what_is_true: The conflict is real. CLAUDE.md:5 and name-screening.md:170 and :188 still say 'must not be orbs', while fighter-concepts-review.md:5 says q3-screen's conditions replaced that line on 2026-09-29. No fragments, keystones or collectibles exist in sim, data, ui or render at HEAD, and the stricter line errs on the safe side.
verdicts.fix: Correct CLAUDE.md:5 and name-screening.md:170 and :188 to point at q3-screen.md's conditions, or record Orb's final choice. Keep the tripwires for when Art draws the fragments.

verdicts.claim: Everything must be original: the fan-recognition test governs every name, design, sound and line; grey-zone defaults apply; fan-game material is off limits; nothing flagged ships; Legal reviews every locked design, name, bark and audio asset.
verdicts.what_is_true: The legal floor (no copied names, characters, art, music or code) is real IP exposure and holds: the franchise name has 0 hits in the live pin's player data, and 'power level' has 0 hits in its UI text. The fan-recognition test, the hair, pose and Easter-egg defaults, and 'no flag open at a phase gate' are Orb's originality direction, stricter than infringement law. The franchise is named in 5 docs/legal files and 4 other docs by choice.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Carrying taste-level margins as release blockers turns every grey-zone call into a phase-gate item and a Legal review.
verdicts.fix: Move the rule to Orb's creative direction, with Legal enforcing only the copying floor, and keep risk-register row 1 for actual copying.
verdicts.belongs_to: Orb's creative direction (Legal for the copying floor)

verdicts.claim: Orb's rule: disclose AI-made content upfront everywhere with one fixed line, in the README and near the top of the holding page; Steam pre-generated yes and live-generated no, itch.io tags; never 'human-made' or 'no AI'; 'computer-controlled opponent', never 'AI opponent'.
verdicts.what_is_true: The disclosure is on README.md:5, the holding page (:21, :33), the /play/ gate, /about/ and the pin's How to play, and no public surface says 'AI opponent', 'no AI' or 'human-made'. Steam's survey does require disclosure of pre-generated content that ships. itch.io strictly enforces only for assets, soundtracks and similar pages and asks games to tag, so Orb's rule goes beyond it, which is fine as Orb's ethic. The /play/ and /about/ text is a variant of the fixed line, not the exact words.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Any kind of content that ships with your game and is consumed by players'
https://itch.io/docs/creators/quality-guidelines (accessed 2026-11-07): 'We ask that you accurately tag your project'
verdicts.fix: Keep it. Record the Steam primary quote (the January 2026 rewording rests on secondary reports), align the /play/ and /about/ wording with the fixed line, and clear C17 in store-copy-draft.md since the README already states it.

verdicts.claim: No asset merges or ships without an origin row in asset-origins.md (and, for audio, a recorded licence); file-level rows are required before a store build; 'edited by Orb' needs the diff; dev tools, CI actions and npm packages are registered.
verdicts.what_is_true: The file-by-file log did stop on 2026-09-29, and the fake EXAMPLE-000 row is still there, but class-level rows cover every class of shipped content. The live index.pck holds only scripts, scenes, JSON and shaders, with no font, audio, image or model file, so no unlogged third-party asset ships. Steam asks for a description of AI content, which the class rows give, so file-level rows are Legal's margin. The tools and npm register part (A8) was not checked.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A 'breached' gate on every merge implies unlicensed assets ship when none do, and file-level rows for thousands of AI-written code files would be busywork.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record to the class-level practice plus a row for any imported third-party file. Write the missing test: fail the site build when the pack holds a font, audio or image file with no register row (packFiles() already reads the pack). Delete EXAMPLE-000.

verdicts.claim: Text from Gemini needs a provenance record kept apart from Orb's lines, complete before main goes public or any store page; Gemini is for creative writing only; the paid consumer app's terms are unconfirmed; no private or NDA material goes into a consumer AI app.
verdicts.what_is_true: Provenance records exist, though still parked under pending: provenance_hw11.json gives the tool, the model as named, the date and a per-line source, and provenance_mc.json has 244 Gemini mentions. Google's Terms of Service (effective 2026-07-30) say Google will not claim ownership of generated content, which answers the consumer-app question. The Gemini-session names Grist and Loupe are in HEAD's fighter_names.json (public repo, LAN builds) but not in the live pin. A provenance row for the naming session was not checked.
external: https://policies.google.com/terms (accessed 2026-11-07, effective 2026-07-30): 'Google won't claim ownership over that content.'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It keeps an 'unconfirmed terms' item and a pre-public gate open after the repo is already public, which prompts more review work.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record with the Google ToS clause, land the two provenance files out of pending, and add a provenance row for the core-four naming session.

verdicts.claim: Shipped music must come from a paid Suno plan through the approved download, with originals and records kept, a separate audio notice, Suno disclosure, no Content ID, a listen check and a lawyer read before sale; other AI audio tools need Legal to read their terms first.
verdicts.what_is_true: Suno's own terms (effective 2026-09-03) confirm Legal's core conditions: free-plan output is personal and non-commercial only, commercial use needs output downloaded through an approved channel, and metadata must stay untouched. No music ships (there is no audio file in the live pack or the tree), and a separate audio/music/NOTICE.txt exists. Legal's screen had read only summaries (suno-music.md:7, :15); the listen check and lawyer read are prudent margins.
external: https://suno.com/terms (accessed 2026-11-07): 'You may not commercially exploit Output that has not been downloaded'
verdicts.fix: Record the primary read of the terms in suno-music.md, have Orb confirm the paid plan before generating a shipped track, and keep the conditions for when music ships.

verdicts.claim: No non-player fighter's stats, rank, looks or behaviour may change from past meetings with the player without Legal first, because of a granted US patent, and a patent attorney reads its claims before the campaign ships or sells.
verdicts.what_is_true: US 10,926,179 is real and, per Google Patents, active with an anticipated expiry of 2036-08-11. The campaign foundation exists at HEAD (sim/core/campaign.gd) behind 'enabled': false and is absent from the live pin, and its header says no fighter reads campaign state (mc01, mc06). The parity check it names was not run.
external: https://patents.google.com/patent/US10926179B2/en (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Nemesis characters, nemesis forts, social vendettas and followers in computer games'
verdicts.fix: Keep it: book the attorney read before the campaign ships or sells, put the patent number in the homework, and cite the parity check that enforces mc01.

verdicts.claim: Every public build's About or licences screen must carry the Godot (MIT) and Open Sans (OFL-1.1) notices, Godot's bundled-library licences, the AI line and a 'Licenses, notices and privacy' link; RL-097 found the notices missing.
verdicts.what_is_true: The notices are required and are in place. The live /about/ page has the Godot MIT line and full text, the Open Sans OFL line and full text, the bundled libraries (FreeType, HarfBuzz, ThorVG and others), the AI line and privacy text, and the /play/ gate links to it as 'Licenses, notices and privacy'. The pin's in-game About carries both notices and a third-party licences page. RL-097 is still Open although fixed.
external: Godot MIT text as served on https://dixonbalsagna.github.io/orb-combat-ex/about/ (accessed 2026-11-07): 'shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software'
verdicts.fix: Close RL-097 (both the notices and the privacy line are fixed), and keep site-licences.json generated from the engine.

verdicts.claim: No outside pull request is merged until the licence is picked and contributor terms, a CONTRIBUTING note and a PR template are in place; contributors sign off under the DCO and state AI help and third-party material.
verdicts.what_is_true: There is no CONTRIBUTING file or PR template, and the public repo states no contribution terms. Nothing has been breached: the repo has had 0 pull requests and 0 forks, and main has one distinct author email. DCO 1.1 is real.
external: https://developercertificate.org/ (accessed 2026-11-07): version 1.1, clause (a) 'created in whole or in part by me'
verdicts.fix: Add a one-line CONTRIBUTING note saying outside pull requests are not accepted until a licence is chosen, and place contributor-rules.md when the licence lands.

verdicts.claim: 'Meridian' is High risk as a public title: CONDITIONAL, working name only, never in store pages, logos, domains or the repo name.
verdicts.what_is_true: The condition is met. The repo is orb-combat-ex, the Pages domain has no 'Meridian', the live pages have 0 hits, the live pack has it only in an allowlisted test fixture, and the README calls it the internal codename. Legal's own rating rests on crowding and protectability. The title moved to Orb Combat EX, yet RL-001 is still an Open P0 gate flag.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: An open P0 gate flag on a satisfied condition adds gate work and makes the Legal backlog look larger than it is.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-001 with a pointer to the pack and page scan. Keep 'Meridian' on never-use-words.md for public copy, and rename the 'Meridian Warden' and 'Meridian Lance' source fields with the KAI rename (S4).

batch_notes: Live checks on 2026-11-07: curl GET of /, /play/, /about/ and /play/index.pck (9,034,688 bytes, Last-Modified 2026-11-05). Running the repo's own tools/site-name-scan.mjs on the live pack gave 0 placeholder hits outside the allowlist. The pack holds only gdc, json, scn, shader, remap and cfg files: no font, audio or image files.
Several A4 rows (RL-001, RL-002, RL-020, RL-097) are still Open although their condition is met on the live site. Marketing's go-to-market-plan.md:31 and :319 still say the live build shows KAI.

Public inaccuracies found along the way: CLAUDE.md:3 says 'Free and open source' with no licence, README.md:7 says the hosted build is offline while /play/ serves a playable build, and the /play/ page title drops '(working title)'.

Commit 701c76a0 (2026-09-29), which is an ancestor of the public origin/main, carries a real-name copyright line in its LICENSE blob and its message. The name is withheld here. It bears on Orb's pseudonym and should go to Orb.
Legal's counsel timing is inconsistent: pre-store-checklist.md:37 says before the store page, while steam-readiness.md:52 says before the first sale, not the page.
